issues.legal_issue: A service-member landlord may use the special eviction remedy even when the tenant occupied the premises before the landlord acquired them, provided the landlord was a landlord while serving and satisfies the remedy’s stated requirements.
material_facts: The landlord was serving in the armed forces when he inherited the flat, which was already occupied by the tenant.
After retirement, the landlord brought a suit under the special provision and produced the required certificate.
The lower authorities found that the landlord bona fide required the flat for his own occupation.
issues.conclusion: The landlord was entitled to seek possession under the special provision despite the tenancy having begun before he became the landlord; he was not required to have personally let the premises to the tenant.
issues.legal_principle: Section 13A-1 of the Bombay Rents, Hotel and Lodging House Rates Control Act, 1947, permits a landlord who was a member of the armed forces and a landlord at the same time to recover premises on proof of bona fide requirement and production of the prescribed certificate. In Mrs. Winifred Ross v. Mrs. Ivy Fonseca, the Court read the provision as requiring the claimant to have been landlord while in service, but the plain text does not further require that the claimant personally created the tenancy. The statement of objects’ phrase “regain possession” means obtain possession, not that the service member must previously have let the premises.

rule.if: special_service_member_eviction_case and landlord_while_serving and required_certificate_produced and bona_fide_need_established and tenant_occupied_before_acquisition

predicates.special_service_member_eviction_case: A landlord who is or was a member of the armed forces brings a special proceeding to recover premises for occupation by the landlord or a family member.
predicates.landlord_while_serving: The claimant was the landlord of the premises during a period when the claimant was serving in the armed forces.
predicates.required_certificate_produced: The landlord produces a service certificate stating the required service status and lack of another suitable residence in the local area.
predicates.bona_fide_need_established: The court finds that the landlord genuinely requires the premises for occupation by the landlord or a family member.
predicates.tenant_occupied_before_acquisition: The tenant was already occupying the premises when the landlord acquired ownership.

issues.definition: When a service-member landlord brings the special eviction proceeding, was a landlord while serving, produces the required certificate, proves bona fide need, and the tenant occupied the premises before acquisition, the landlord may recover despite that preexisting tenancy.

issues.legal_issue: Under the special eviction remedy for service members, a landlord who produces the prescribed certificate and proves bona fide need need not establish comparative hardship against the tenant.
material_facts: The landlord produced the prescribed certificate in the special eviction suit.
The lower authorities concurrently found that he bona fide required the premises for his own occupation.
The High Court set aside the eviction decree on a different ground, and the Supreme Court restored the lower authorities’ decree.
issues.conclusion: Once the certificate requirement and bona fide requirement are satisfied, the landlord is entitled to recover possession without proving that refusal to evict would cause greater hardship to the landlord than eviction would cause to the tenant.
issues.legal_principle: Section 13A-1 creates a special route distinct from the general grounds under Section 13(1)(g) and the comparative-hardship safeguard in Section 13(2). The prescribed certificate is conclusive evidence of the stated service status and absence of another suitable local residence; it does not establish bona fide need, which the landlord must prove separately. Once bona fide need is established, Section 13A-1 does not require a comparative-hardship finding.
